Searching 200 factors and reporting the best without correction would have produced a Sharpe of 0.68 (t = 1.91).
The corrected tests above ask a different question: whether ANY factor in the searched universe has skill, given that the best of many was selected.
Nothing survives. That is the expected outcome of a search this size over a series this short, and it is the result -- not a failure to find one.
Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016) argue that t > 3.0 is the right bar for a published factor once the profession's collective search is counted. This search alone was 200 wide.
